notes.text: pre-training -> training -> post-training
datasets: scraping the internet. FineWeb: decanting the web for the finest text data at scale (huggingface.co/spaces/HuggingFaceFW/blogpost-fineweb-v1)

tokenisation: the process of converting some text into tokens. look like numbers but they are essentially unique ids, symbols for that text. each token can be a word, a slice of word, some words, phrase, whitespace, punctuation - anything is possible. visualised here: tiktokenizer.vercel.app
context - sequence of tokens. context window - maximum it can hold

parameters (8B parameters in Qwen / LLama is how many weights it has). used during training: similar to knobs on a DJ set. weights for the mathematical expressions which form the neural network. we keep tweaking the weights until the predictions are correct outputs
transformer is a type of deep learning neural network architecture. take input -> go through a transformer -> get output. neural network: bbycroft.net/llm
inference (didnt understand this much). the job of predicting the next token for any given token. token -> neural network -> (probabilities) -> sample -> next token

Token vs Vector (Embedding = a vector with a meaning/representation) — understood at a high level but not very clear. a token is just an ID, like a lookup key. It has no meaning by itself. The model then looks up that ID and gets an embedding, which is just a list of numbers. That's where meaning starts to live. Same word, different sentences, the transformer updates that list based on surrounding words
Temperature = how much tolerance we have with the probability. low temperature = higher accuracy
So what is a base model? xx parameters trained on yy tokens. Llama 3 (2024) is 405 billion parameters trained on 15 million tokens
